ideas.title: The Anchoring Number Trap
ideas.angle: An interactive test where I make you guess the price of a luxury watch after showing you a high number. It proves how stores use 'Anchoring' to make $100 look cheap by showing $1000 first. Viewers will comment their guesses to see how close they were.

hook.en: I’m about to control your brain.

ideas.reason: Interactive 'mind control' videos have the highest retention. The Anchoring Effect is a cornerstone of behavioral economics used by Apple and Rolex to justify high prices.
sources: Thinking, Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman
Journal of Marketing Research on Price Anchoring

ideas.title: The Decoy Option Trick
ideas.angle: A live challenge showing three popcorn sizes. It explains why the 'Medium' exists only to make the 'Large' look like a steal. It forces the viewer to pick an option in their head, then reveals why they were manipulated. Comment trigger: 'What did you pick?'

hook.en: You’re being robbed by the medium.

ideas.reason: The Decoy Effect (Asymmetric Dominance) is currently trending in 'Dark Marketing' circles. It exploits the human inability to judge absolute value.

ideas.title: The Sunk Cost Trap
ideas.angle: A high-speed scenario showing why you finish a bad movie or keep a losing stock. It explains 'Loss Aversion'—why your brain hates losing $10 more than it loves winning $20. Ends with a 'Stop doing this' command to save money.

hook.en: Stop wasting money on bad choices.

ideas.reason: Financial 'truth-telling' content is seeing a 40% surge in engagement. Loss aversion is a primal survival mechanism that now ruins modern bank accounts.
sources: The Psychology of Money by Morgan Housel
Harvard Business Review on Sunk Cost Fallacy
